awards.display_name: THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY A POPULATION OF COMPACT SUPERMASSIVE BLACK HOLE BINARIES (SMBHBS) IN GALACTIC NUCLEI. SMBHBS ARE BELIEVED TO FORM FREQUENTLY IN GALAXY MERGERS  AND ARE A FUNDAMENTAL INGREDIENT IN THE HIERARCHICAL ASSEMBLY OF GALAXIES. THEY ARE ALSO PRIME TARGETS FOR ON-GOING AND PLANNED GRAVITATIONAL WAVE EXPERIMENTS  DESIGNED TO TEST OUR FUNDAMENTAL UNDERSTANDING OF GRAVITY. WE WILL ANALYZE ARCHIVAL UV  X-RAY  AND IR OBSERVATIONS  TO TEST THE BINARY HYPOTHESIS FOR A SAMPLE OF APPROXIMATELY 150 QUASARS  NEWLY IDENTIFIED AS BINARY CANDIDATES BASED ON PERIODICITIES IN THEIR OPTICAL LIGHT-CURVES. WE WILL TEST THE RELATIONS PREDICTED BY BINARY MODELS BETWEEN THE OPTICAL  UV AND X-RAY PERIODICITES (ALL DIRECTLY PRODUCED IN THE ACCRETION DISKS NEAR THE BHS)  AND THEIR IR LIGHT ECHOES (PRODUCED FARTHER OUT IN A DUSTY CIRCUMBINARY TORUS). WE WILL CAREFULLY COMPARE OUR FINDINGS WITH A SUITABLY DESIGNED CONTROL SAMPLE OF NON-PERIODIC QUASARS WITH SIMILAR PROPERTIES. WE WILL INTEPRET THE INFERRED ABUNDANCE OF BINARIES BY COMPARING THEM TO THEORETICAL MODELS FOR THE UNDERLYING SMBHB POPULATION. FINALLY  WE WILL PERFORM FOLLOW-UP OPTICAL OBSERVATIONS OF THE MOST PROMISING CANDIDATES. THIS PROPOSAL WILL SUBSTANTIALLY LEVERAGE RECENT THEORETICAL WORK  INCLUDING PREDICTIONS BY OUR OWN GROUP FOR PERIODIC VISIBLE  UV AND X-RAY SIGNALS FROM BINARIES THROUGH HYDRODYNAMICAL ACCRETION RATE FLUCTUATIONS AND THROUGH RELATIVISTIC DOPPLER BOOSTING. THE RESULTS WILL BE APPLIED TO SMBHB CANDIDATES IDENTIFIED OVER THE PAST YEAR. OUR PROPOSAL WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT NASA'S STRATEGIC PLAN  SUB- GOAL 3D: "DISCOVER THE ORIGIN  STRUCTURE  EVOLUTION AND DESTINY OF THE UNIVERSE AND SEARCH FOR EARTH-LIKE PLANETS".
